title: Fall from rest in curved level profiles: curvature terms and local slope

key_results.statement: For every level block with quadratic level profiles ($\zeta=1$), weak records, first order in slopes and curvatures: the upper-branch acceleration operator is $\hat A=a(p)+\frac12\{b(p),\eta\}$, where $a$ is $a_{k,+}$ of (4.7) at $g_{\zeta,k}=0$ and $b$ is the same function with $(G,\mathcal F)\to(H,\mathcal H)$, i.e. the linear-profile acceleration with local slopes $G+H\eta$, $\mathcal F+\mathcal H\eta$ (explicit form in (15.8)).

For every such block and every start $B_{k,+}[g]$ centred at $x_0$ with finite $W$, at first order (fixed $\lambda$, start, chain; then long chain): $\mathrm d^2\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda^2=\langle a\rangle_g+c_g+\lambda\langle b\omega'\rangle_g+A_{\rm osc}(\lambda)+O(\varepsilon^2)$, $c_g=\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}bj$, with $A_{\rm osc}=-8\operatorname{Re}\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}\omega^2e^{2i\omega\lambda}f$ bounded in $\lambda$; the non-oscillating part is exactly linear in $\lambda$.

For every such block and every start $B_{k,+}[g]$ centred at $x_0$, the block $S_{-+}$ of the first-order block-diagonalizing generator is explicit (15.15), so the oscillating amplitude $f=-i\alpha g^*(S_{-+}g)$ is explicit; at every $\tau/M$, $v_{\rm osc}\le\frac{2\tau^2}{M^2}(\sigma_0+\sigma_1W+\sigma_2W_4^2)$ and $\lvert A_{\rm osc}(\lambda)\rvert\le\frac{4\tau^2}{M}(\sigma_0+\sigma_1W+\sigma_2W_4^2)$ for all $\lambda$, with $\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ linear in the slopes and curvatures and $W_4^2=\lVert\eta^2g\rVert$ (15.16); $W_4$ is an auxiliary envelope width, not the body's position fourth moment $W_{4,\rm ph}^4=\langle\psi_0\vert\hat y^4\vert\psi_0\rangle$, and $W_4^2\le W_{4,\rm ph}^2+r^2/4$, $r=\tau/M$, so these bounds, (15.11) and the sufficient conditions of (15.11)–(15.12) remain valid with $W_4^2$ replaced by $W_{4,\rm ph}^2+r^2/4$.

The curvatures contribute $c_g+\lambda\langle b\omega'\rangle_g$ to the non-oscillating acceleration, which contains $\eta g$ only linearly and has no $W^2$ term, and to $A_{\rm osc}$ a part bounded uniformly in $\lambda$ that depends on the start through $\eta g$ and $\eta^2g$, at most $\frac{4\tau^2}{M}(\sigma_0+\sigma_1W+\sigma_2W_4^2)$ at $G=\mathcal F=0$; the contribution grows linearly in $\lambda$ iff $\langle b\omega'\rangle_g\ne0$; at rest $\lvert c_g\rvert\le\frac12b_2\kappa_4^{1/2}\delta p^2W$, $\lvert\langle b\omega'\rangle_g\rvert\le\frac16b_3\kappa_4^{1/2}\delta p^3$; $c_g=0$ if $j\equiv0$, $\langle b\omega'\rangle_g=0$ if $\lvert g\rvert^2$ is even.

For starts at rest centred at $x_0$, the window average of the first-order acceleration (length $\Lambda$, centre $\lambda_c$) differs from $a(0)=\frac{\tau^2}{M}(\mathcal F-G)$ by at most $\frac12a_2\delta p^2+\frac12b_2\kappa_4^{1/2}\delta p^2W+\frac16b_3\kappa_4^{1/2}\delta p^3\lvert\lambda_c\rvert+\frac{4\tau^2}{M^2\Lambda}(\sigma_0+\sigma_1W+\sigma_2W_4^2)$; relative error $\epsilon$ (for $a(0)\ne0$) if each term is at most $\epsilon\lvert a(0)\rvert/4$ (sufficient), for the last term the window condition $M\Lambda\ge16(\sigma_0+\sigma_1W+\sigma_2W_4^2)/(\epsilon\lvert\mathcal F-G\rvert)$ at every $\tau/M$.

For starts at rest centred at $x_0$ with even $\lvert g\rvert^2$: $\lim_{\delta p\to0}\lim_{\Lambda\to\infty}\bar A_\Lambda=\frac{\tau^2}{M}(\mathcal F-G)$ exactly at first order along families with $\kappa_4$ bounded and $\delta p^2W\to0$, after first order and the long chain; for windows $[\lambda_1,\lambda_1+\Lambda]$ at fixed start the inner limit exists iff $\langle b\omega'\rangle_g=0$, otherwise a joint limit with $\Lambda_n\delta p_n^3\to0$ and $(1+W_n+W_{4,n}^2)/\Lambda_n\to0$ gives the same value; such $\Lambda_n$ exist iff $(1+W_n+W_{4,n}^2)\delta p_n^3\to0$, which holds when $W_n\delta p_n$ and $W_{4,n}\delta p_n$ stay bounded, in particular when $W_n\delta p_n$ and $W_{4,{\rm ph},n}\delta p_n$ stay bounded.

Factor class $M_{x,k}=(m+d_k)n_x$, $V=0$, $\tau_k=\tau$, $N\ge2$: for $g_n\ne0$ or $h_n\ne0$ there are starts of the class for which the non-oscillating first-order acceleration differs between levels, leading difference $g_n\tau^4(M_k^{-2}-M_l^{-2})\delta p^2$ for $j\equiv0$ and even $\lvert g\rvert^2$ (hopping not multiplied by $n_x$); in the limit (15.12) it is level-independent, $-g_n\tau^2$.
Control $M_{x,k}=m\,n_x+d_k$: for $g_n\ne0$ not level-independent already in the limit (15.12), $a_k(0)-a_l(0)=\tau^2mg_n(d_k-d_l)/((m+d_k)(m+d_l))$, of zeroth order in $\delta p$.

open_issues: First order is not uniform in λ (the non-oscillating mean position contains a λ³ term); long falls and second order are out of scope.
In the factor class the level dependence at δp > 0 comes from the unscaled hopping; whether a common factor on the hopping (ζ ≠ 1) removes it is out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: all terms of the first-order acceleration have dimension [C]², λ ~ [C]⁻¹, position label dimensionless
Zero curvatures: b = 0, the non-oscillating acceleration is ⟨a_{k,+}⟩_g of (4.7) and (15.12) reduces to (4.11) with a(0) of (4.16)
τ → 0: a = b = f = 0, the first-order acceleration vanishes, as the exact [C, x̂] = 0 requires
